<description>
Clarifies the `addnode` RPC help on the separate limits for `add` and `onetry`: `add` entries are capped by `MAX_ADDNODE_CONNECTIONS`, `onetry` connections are not.

Also fixes `-netinfo`: the manual peer count is `uint8_t` while the other counts are `uint16_t`, so it wraps at 256. This is reachable via `addnode onetry`, which is not subject to the `MAX_ADDNODE_CONNECTIONS` cap.
</description>

<commits>
e46bcd40bb cli: use uint16_t for -netinfo manual peer count

The other -netinfo peer counts are uint16_t, but the manual peer count
was uint8_t and wraps at 256. Manual peers aren't limited to the 8
-addnode slots (addnode onetry connections also count as manual and are
not subject to MAX_ADDNODE_CONNECTIONS), so the count can reach that and
the "manual" column then disappears or shows a wrapped value.

4c4970a696 rpc: clarify addnode 'add' vs 'onetry' connection limits

Persistent addnode connections added with the 'add' command are capped at
MAX_ADDNODE_CONNECTIONS, while 'onetry' connections are not subject to
that limit. Say so in the addnode RPC help.
</commits>

                     {"v2transport", RPCArg::Type::BOOL, RPCArg::DefaultHint{"set by -v2transport"}, "Attempt to connect using BIP324 v2 transport protocol (ignored for 'remove' command)"},
